title: Fermat Torricelli
comment: Fermat Torricelli — The Fermat-Torricelli point minimizes the sum of the distance to the vertices of a triangle. If the angles are less than 120°, can be computed by forming three equilateral triangles, otherwise it is one of the vertices. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat_point

title: Dct
comment: Dct — Discrete Cosine Transforms are eigenvectors of Laplacians with different boundary conditions. Wonderful paper by Strang. http://www-math.mit.edu/~gs/papers/dct.pdf

title: Brownian
comment: Brownian — A Brownian motion is approximated by a discrete random walk with Gaussian increments. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownian_motion
alt_text: Brownian. A Brownian motion is approximated by a discrete random walk with Gaussian increments.

title: Shatten Norms
comment: Shatten Norms — Schatten p-norms are the l^p norms of the singular values. Define algebra norm invariant by isometries. Generalizes the nuclear norm (p=1), Frobenius norm (p=2) and the operator norm (p=inf). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schatten_norm
alt_text: Shatten Norms. Schatten p-norms are the l^p norms of the singular values. Define algebra norm invariant by isometries. Generalizes the nuclear norm (p=1), Frobenius norm (p=2) and the operator norm (p=inf).

title: Reeb Graph
comment: Reeb Graph — The Reeb graph of a function on a manifold is the graph of level sets ordered by inclusion. For a 2D function (an image), it is the contour graph, and is actually a directed tree (polytree). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reeb_graph
alt_text: Reeb Graph. The Reeb graph of a function on a manifold is the graph of level sets ordered by inclusion. For a 2D function (an image), it is the contour graph, and is actually a directed tree (polytree).

title: Perceptron
comment: Perceptron — A 1 hidden layer perceptron can approximate arbitrary continuous functions using a large enough number of neurons (Cybenko's theorem). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_approximation_theorem
alt_text: Perceptron. A 1 hidden layer perceptron can approximate arbitrary continuous functions using a large enough number of neurons (Cybenko's theorem).

title: Subdiff
comment: Subdiff — The subdifferential is the set of slopes bellow the graph of a convex function. It is a set-valued monotone map. Generalize the gradient to non-smooth functions. The most fundamental tool of non-smooth convex analysis. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subderivative
alt_text: Subdiff. The subdifferential is the set of slopes bellow the graph of a convex function. It is a set-valued monotone map. Generalize the gradient to non-smooth functions. The most fundamental tool of non-smooth convex analysis.

title: Eikonale
comment: Eikonale — The distance field is the unique viscosity solution of the Eikonale equation. Pierre-Louis Lions got the Fields medal in 1994 in part for this concept. https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.jmsj/1230130200
alt_text: Eikonale. The distance field is the unique viscosity solution of the Eikonale equation. Pierre-Louis Lions got the Fields medal in 1994 in part for this concept.

title: Flow Manifold
comment: Flow Manifold — The integral curves of a vector field tangent to a manifold stays on the manifold. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integral_curve

title: Manifold
comment: Manifold — A Riemannian manifold is locally an Euclidean space. An embedded surface (e.g. the Earth) is an example. It defines a Riemannian tensors field (first fundamental form) in parametric space which encode length deformations. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemannian_manifold

title: Mean Curvature
comment: Mean Curvature — The mean curvature motion is the most fundamental curve evolution. It is the equivalent for curves of the heat equation. It is independent of parameterisation (intrinsic) and minimizes the length of the curve (shortening flow). It… https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curve-shortening_flow
alt_text: Mean Curvature. The mean curvature motion is the most fundamental curve evolution. It is the equivalent for curves of the heat equation. It is independent of parameterisation (intrinsic) and minimizes the length of the curve (shortening flow). It shrinks the curves toward an ellipse.

title: Continued Fraction
